agent_prediction.rationale:
## Top-line call: Antonelli wins, Norris P2, Russell P3.

The quantitative models split: Stage 9 weights recent finishes heavily and crowns Norris (46% win) on the back of his P2-P2 form, while Stage 6's calibration-first prior keeps Antonelli (31% win) on top. The composite splits the difference (Norris 32.6% / Antonelli 30.6% / Verstappen 14.8% / Piastri 16.2% / Russell 15.5%). Three judgments push me toward Antonelli rather than the composite's nominal leader:

1. **Momentum is non-modeled.** Antonelli has won three straight (China, Japan, Miami) and now leads the championship by 20 points. Stage 9's recency window captures finishing position but not the qualitative "current performance gap" â€” Mercedes has clearly been the fastest package over the last three weekends. Miami pole + win after a polesitter scrap with Verstappen / Leclerc reinforces that the W17 is the reference car right now, not a fluke.
2. **Mercedes is a Montreal team.** Russell won from pole here in 2025 and Antonelli took his maiden podium in the same race. The track's stop-start layout (long straights + tight hairpin + slow chicanes) rewards traction and braking stability â€” Mercedes' two strong suits this year. Russell P3 reflects the same logic, just demoted because Antonelli has the upper hand intra-team in 2026.
3. **Norris stays in podium contention but the win is asking a lot.** McLaren's MCL40 was second-quickest at Miami but couldn't actually pass Antonelli on track, even with Norris running a fresher tyre window. Stage 9 is essentially extrapolating his back-to-back P2s without pricing in that he's been losing to one specific car â€” and the gap doesn't shrink unless something changes (weather, reliability). I keep him P2.

**Sprint-weekend caveat.** R5 is a sprint format, which adds variance: Saturday sprint points can scramble starting confidence, and a wet sprint (light rain in the forecast) could disrupt setup choices. If conditions go fully wet on Sunday, Verstappen and Hamilton become live podium threats â€” but I'm not pricing rain as the modal outcome.

**Where I differ from the composite top 10.** I demote Hadjar (composite has him P8 at 2% win â€” too high without a confirming recent result) and lift Bearman (Haas had two P11-P13 finishes; Montreal historically rewards Haas race pace). I keep Sainz P10 â€” Williams has been a midfield-fringe team and Sainz has been their reliable scorer.
